preamble: Clues are listed in alphabetical order of their solutions. These are to be fitted into the grid, jigsaw-wise, in such a way that the middle letters of the central down solution, followed by seven words running clockwise round the circumference from the top left-hand corner, together spell out my promised intention.

clue.text: Female artist talked of member in congress?

indicators.note: talked of means the two names are said out loud, and what we hear is the answer

parts.note: an invented woman painter, Polly Titian: Polly is a woman's name and Titian the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: Gossip about a woman painter who is rumoured to sit in a legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly Titian, said quickly, is POLITICIAN. The question mark flags that congress here means a law-making assembly such as the US Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislator sitting in a national assembly like the US Congress is, by profession, a politician.

clue.text: Too fond of wife in Egyptian city going topless (very good topless)

indicators.note: a city going topless loses its first letter, the top of a down entry

parts.note: Luxor is the Nile city on the site of ancient Thebes

indicators.note: the second topless again strips the opening letter from the word for very good

parts.note: pious, devout and virtuous, is very good in the moral sense

explanation.surface: A doting husband visits Luxor, where the bathing turns out to be topless.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis is a separate instruction, so both pieces lose their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorious describes a husband who shows excessive devotion to his spouse.

clue.text: Playing a lute wearing jeans? On the contrary, suited for the small screen

indicators.note: wearing puts one thing around another, as clothes surround a body
the reversal of roles: the jumbled letters wear the jeans, not the other way round
playing the letters of a lute rearranges them like notes

parts.note: the words a lute are taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange
Levi's is the famous brand of denim jeans

explanation.surface: A lutenist in denim performing, perhaps auditioning for a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: On the contrary swaps the container: the scrambled A LUTE goes round LEVIS, not LEVIS round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Televisual means relating to or well suited to television, the small screen.

clue.text: First-class drug, working for a long time

parts.note: A, as in A1 or grade A, is first-class
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone on a top-grade stimulant has been grinding away for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immensely long period, an age beyond counting.

clue.text: Good headgear for Indian flight?

parts.note: a hat is the obvious piece of headgear

explanation.surface: Asking for a good hat to wear on an Indian plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight means a flight of steps, not an air journey: a ghat is a set of steps down to a river in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a ghat is a broad stairway leading down to a riverbank, used for bathing.

clue.text: Moved very slowly, having wrongly taken piano away

indicators.note: taken ... away surrounds the thing removed, so the soft-music letter drops out
completes taken away, the instruction to remove a piece

parts.note: something taken wrongly has been stolen, or pinched

explanation.surface: A removal man shuffles along after stealing a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Inched means crept forward by tiny amounts, an inch at a time.

clue.text: Football club in Warwickshire, allegedly

indicators.note: in points to letters sitting inside the next two words, across the comma

parts.note: the last two letters of Warwickshire and the first two of allegedly run together

explanation.surface: A rumour that some football club is based in Warwickshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of Warwickshire and the start of allegedly. Real is short for Real Madrid, the Spanish club.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid, often just called Real, is one of the world's best-known football clubs.

clue.text: Trick taking 30 minutes? Answer: 10 more needed

parts.note: thirty minutes is half an hour, so half of the word hour
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A con that takes half an hour, with the punchline that ten more minutes are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of HOUR gives HO; the answer abbreviation A and Roman ten complete it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deceptive trick played on someone.

clue.text: Just the day before name's first given

parts.note: eve is the day before a festival, as Christmas Eve

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word name

parts.note: the word name, whose first letter alone is used
handed means passed over, given

explanation.surface: A name was assigned only the day before, as if a baby were registered late.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-handed means fair and impartial, which is what just means here.

clue.text: Prayer time in church after row

indicators.note: after places the church letters following the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: When prayers begin in church after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Row rhymes with cow here (a tier of seats), not with how. Tierce is the canonical hour of mid-morning prayer, also spelt terce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tierce is the third canonical hour, the office of prayer said around 9am.

clue.text: Bananas the man will briefly put in fruit container

parts.note: bananas means crazy, as does nuts
he will, contracted, is he'll

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to drop bananas into a fruit bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas is not fruit here but madness.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut's hard shell encloses its kernel, the fruit, so it is a natural container.

clue.text: US law is somewhat eccentric, only found in two states

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used, a run of their letters

parts.note: the final three letters of eccentric and the first of only run together

explanation.surface: A complaint that some odd American statute applies in just two states.
explanation.walkthrough: As a bonus, two states give the answer too: RI is Rhode Island and CO Colorado.
explanation.definitionFit: The RICO Act is the US federal statute against racketeering and organised crime.

clue.text: Cancel home TV licence, when discontented with Aida production?

parts.note: at home is in

indicators.note: a production of an opera reworks it, so these letters are staged in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: discontented means with its contents removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the word licence, of which only the first and last letters survive
Verdi's opera, taken as written

explanation.surface: Scrapping the TV licence in disgust at a staging of Verdi's Aida.
explanation.walkthrough: The British TV licence is the annual fee that funds the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: To invalidate something is to annul it or make it void.

clue.text: Football club house criminal that's homeless

indicators.note: homeless means the word for at home is taken away

parts.note: a villain is a criminal

explanation.surface: A football club's mansion turns out to belong to a homeless crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Football club is a second definition: Aston Villa, the Birmingham club.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or suburban house.

clue.text: Landlord, male, wearing hairstyle that might cause trouble at opening time

definitions.text: that might cause trouble at opening time

parts.note: a landlord lets property, so is a letter

indicators.note: wearing means the hairstyle goes round the male letter

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut

explanation.surface: A pub landlord with an odd haircut causes a scene when the pub opens.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening time looks like pub hours, but it means opening the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter bomb is an explosive device that detonates when the envelope is opened.

clue.text: Finished with Hilary? End it with a falling-out

parts.note: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford and in the law courts

indicators.note: a falling-out is a quarrel that scatters things, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words end it are taken letter for letter for the rearranging
the article a joins the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is done with a friend called Hilary and wants to end it with a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is not a friend here but an academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminated means brought to an end, finished.

clue.text: Tunes broadcast by soprano

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Songs put out on radio, sung by a soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Airs are melodies or songs.

clue.text: Among body of soldiers left in the dark

indicators.note: among puts the letter for left inside the soldiers' word

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A soldier left alone in the dark among his platoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without light, so in darkness.

clue.text: Pub run by Epstein's partner, going viral

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub run by the partner of a man called Epstein becomes an internet sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: Epstein-Barr is the virus behind glandular fever, named after its discoverers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvonne Barr co-discovered the Epstein-Barr virus, so her name is joined to Epstein's.

clue.text: Bishop with a note left behind by Kate Bush's first nanny in Russia

indicators.note: first places the singer's surname before what remains of her first name

parts.note: the article a is used just as it stands
the singer's surname Bush, taken as written

indicators.note: the note is left behind by Kate, so it drops out of her name

parts.note: the singer's first name Kate, from which a note is removed
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A churchman leaves a musical note from singer Kate Bush with a Russian nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanny means granny here, the word's informal British sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Babushka is the Russian word for grandmother, and a nanny is informally a grandmother.

clue.text: One of two Spice Girls in cooking area, with new decorated kitchen items

indicators.note: in places the Spice Girl inside the jumbled letters
cooking signals the letters being stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the word area is taken letter for letter for the cooking
the word new joins the letters being stirred together
Mel B and Mel C were both Spice Girls, so either is a Mel

explanation.surface: A pop star in a kitchen, surrounded by new decorated pans.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamelware is cookware coated in enamel, often patterned.

clue.text: Rodent holding up two male animals

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tom is a male cat and a ram a male sheep

explanation.surface: A rodent supports a pair of male beasts on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmot is a large ground squirrel, a burrowing rodent.

clue.text: Vivacity shown by Hungarian writer after change of heart

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its middle, and those letters are swapped round

parts.note: the biro, the ballpoint pen, is named after its Hungarian inventor Laszlo Biro

explanation.surface: A Hungarian author who has had a change of heart and now writes with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is a pen, not a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vigour and liveliness.

clue.text: Coming out of WC shortly after one on throne pinches me

indicators.note: after places the cut-down toilet word last
pinches means the royal letters squeeze the word me between them

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the word me is used just as it stands

indicators.note: shortly means cut short by the last letter

parts.note: in Britain, the Gents is the men's toilet

explanation.surface: Emerging from the loo after the monarch on the throne gives you a pinch.
explanation.walkthrough: The throne is a toilet in the surface but a royal seat in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent describes something emerging or coming into being.

clue.text: Academic books written by doctor

indicators.note: in a down entry, by means next to, so the books go below the doctor

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Scholarly books produced by a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is academic: open to debate but of no practical consequence.

clue.text: Elder twin brother from eastern half of 5

indicators.note: half of means just the second three of its six letters are kept

parts.note: clue 5 in the printed list is the capital of Guinea-Bissau

explanation.surface: An older twin hailing from the east side of an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 is the fifth clue in the printed alphabetical list, the capital answer; its eastern half is its right-hand half.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau was the first-born of Isaac's twin sons, Jacob being the younger.

clue.text: Group of players wanting tennis's No 1 place Andy Murray finally won

indicators.note: number one means only the opening letter of tennis

parts.note: the word tennis, whose first letter alone is used
Murray won his second Olympic gold at Rio in 2016

explanation.surface: A band lacking its top tennis player, at the venue where Murray triumphed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wanting means lacking: three players without their first letter leave the Olympic city.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three musicians performing together.

clue.text: Capital returns from chihuahua's siblings

indicators.note: returns means the letters are read backwards
from tells us to take letters within the words that follow

parts.note: the end of chihuahua's and the start of siblings hold the letters, to be read backwards

explanation.surface: Money comes back from a chihuahua's littermates.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital is a city, not money: Bissau is the capital of Guinea-Bissau.
explanation.definitionFit: Bissau is the capital city of the West African state Guinea-Bissau.

clue.text: Voluntary fee after working topless for one man-hour

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order
topless means the first letter of the word for is removed

parts.note: the word for, which loses its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tip for an hour's labour, given after working without a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorarium is a payment for services given as a courtesy, where no fee is formally required.

clue.text: Cry as doll is pierced with end of needle

indicators.note: the doll's name is pierced, so a letter goes inside it

parts.note: Ken is Barbie's boyfriend doll

indicators.note: end of means just the final letter of needle

parts.note: the word needle, whose last letter alone is used

explanation.surface: Someone wails as a doll is stabbed with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief for the dead, as in an Irish lament.
